hook: In 1727, Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II built India's first planned city.

sections.voiceover: In 1727, Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II built India's first planned city.
b_roll: Historical map of Rajasthan showing Jaipur in 1727

sections.voiceover: Kachwaha rulers moved their capital 9 kilometers from hilltop Amer. NASA Earth Observatory notes the shift covered 11 kilometers from Amber. Why did the plan split Jaipur into 9 rectangular sectors?
b_roll: Map showing 9 km distance from hilltop Amer to Jaipur
NASA Earth Observatory satellite view of Amber and Jaipur

sections.voiceover: However, congestion meant Amber couldn't remain the capital, so rulers chose a plain in Rajasthan.
b_roll: Grid overlay highlighting roads intersecting at right angles

sections.voiceover: UNESCO documented the walled city layout in Rajasthan. Sawai Jai Singh II based the grid on Vedic architecture. Straight roads divided the city into 9 distinct urban sectors.
b_roll: UNESCO World Heritage documentation graphics of walled Jaipur
High-angle view of straight roads forming 9 sectors

sections.voiceover: Jaipur remains India's planned grid city built in 1727.
b_roll: Panoramic graphic of modern walled Jaipur grid layout
